top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct, mature and reproduced achievement: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the lattice light shift while many atoms are held in the Lamb-Dicke regime, giving fast averaging and systematic uncertainty near 10^-18, verified by independent clocks agreeing across laboratories and already opening tests of gravitational redshift, drifting constants and dark matter. Katori (invention and first strontium lattice clock) and Ye (realization at the accuracy and stability frontier) are two necessary steps of one achievement, and the citation scope around invention and realization fits within the two-name allocation. Awarding it is clearly better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; as WACQT director and a superconducting-circuits theorist I have no direct tie to Katori or Ye, though Chalmers hosts broad precision-measurement and quantum-technology contacts.
